text:
jess: FYI - sample-app edge build surfaced wacky typing breaks. Generics stop inferring when we bundle to ESM for edge runtimes. Anyone run into this pattern?

aiden: yep. usually a combo of positional overloads + middleware-augmented opts. TS picks the wrong overload after emit or when types are resolved through an exports/type subpath.

jess: minimal repro:
```ts
export function call(auth: string, opts?: Opts): Promise<R>
export function call(opts: Opts): Promise<R>
export function call(a: any, b?: any) { /* impl */ }
export function createClient<T = unknown>(opts: ClientOpts<T>) { /* ... */ }
```
Calling `createClient({ auth: token, retry: { count: 2 } })` in edge sample becomes `any` for `T`.

rachel: two fast wins: 1) avoid exporting middleware-augmented intersections (use a private symbol for retry metadata), 2) ensure sample-app tsconfig uses `module: "ESNext"` and `moduleResolution: "bundler"`.

aiden: also check package.json exports/types. Edge consumers rely on the `import` path and sometimes the types subpath. Example: 
```json
"exports": {".": {"import": "./dist/esm/index.js","require": "./dist/cjs/index.js","types": "./dist/types/index.d.ts"}}
```
and add `typesVersions` for modern TS if you need different d.ts for ESM/CJS.

jess: we did `skipLibCheck: true` and changed to object-style params locally and that fixed inference. But we can't break public API. Any non-breaking tricks?

rachel: brand the auth param so the intended overload is unambiguous: `type AuthBrand = string & { __authBrand?: never }`. Or keep overloads but move the most specific signature first. Both are non-breaking at runtime.

aiden: temporary remediation: callsite cast `createClient({ auth: token }) as Client<MyType>` and patch sample-app CI to run `tsc --noEmit` with both CJS+ESM declarations. Then open a gradual SDK issue to migrate to object-param form.

jess: thanks. One last gotcha: we saw `TS1259` about default imports when esModuleInterop is off. Edge bundles want `allowSyntheticDefaultImports: true` and keep `esModuleInterop: false`. Make sure your published package doesn't rely on synthetic defaults in its d.ts.

devx-bot: created ticket: js-sdk#318 "Edge ESM builds: overload inference + middleware metadata" and added ESM+edge job to sample-app CI. :robot_face:

aiden: ok I'll draft a short PR with: branded overload, symbol-based retry metadata, tsconfig update in sample-app, and a CI typing job.
jess: perfect — will review.
